texts.preamble: Raju vs Sanjay on 23 March, 2024 :1: In The Court Of Ms. Charu Gupta Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01 (Se), Saket Courts : New Delhi Mact No. : 516/22 Raju Vs. Sanjay & Ors. Cnr No. Dlse01-006615-2022 1. Sh. Raju S/o Sh. Som Prakash R/o A-1/457, Jj colony, Block A-1, Madanpur Khadar, Sarita Vihar, New Delhi-110076. ....Claimant/Petitioner Versus 1. Sanjay S/o Sh. Joginder Singh R/o Village-Alipur, Ballabhgarh Faridabad, Haryana. ....Driver-cum-owner/Respondent no.1 2. Iffco Tokyo General Insurance Company Iffco Tower, 4th & 5th Floor, Plot no.3, Sector-29, Gurgaon, Haryana-122001. ....Insurance/Respondent no.2 Date of accident : 24.06.2022 Date of filing of petition : 20.07.2022 Date of Decision : 23.03.2024 Mact No. 516/22 Raju v. Sanjay & Ors . Page no. 1 of 24 Bk Award 1.
texts.facts: In this case, a claim petition u/s 166 (1) Motor Vehicle Act was initially filed. Subsequently a Detailed Accident Report was filed u/s 158(6) of Motor Vehicle Act by the IO, upon which the DAR was clubbed with the claim petition. Raju vs Sanjay on 23 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55324884/ 1 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 24.06.2022 at around 12:30 PM, an accident took place at Okhla NSIC, Metro Station in which the petitioner /claimant Raju, while riding his bicycle was allegedly hit by a truck bearing no. HR-38U-4255 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle). It is alleged that the offending vehicle was being driven in a rash and negligent manner. It is alleged that due to the accident, petitioner/claimant sustained grievous injuries resulting in amputation of his left arm (below the elbow) and left leg (below the knee). The accident was reported through a PCR call and consequently an FIR no. 0441 dated 24.06.2022, u/s 279/337 of IPC was registered at PS Kalkaji. Police investigated the matter and filed a chargesheet u/s 279/338 of IPC. 3. As per record, the offending vehicle is owned as well as was being driven by Respondent no. 1 and Insured with Respondent no. 2/Insurance company. Respondent no. 2 filed its reply refuting its liability. As per the reply, involvement of the offending vehicle, existence of a valid driving licence and permit in favour of Respondent no.1 is disputed. It is further pleaded that the victim /petitioner contributed to the accident and hence is not entitled to claim compensation. 4. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were MACT No. 516/22 Raju v. Sanjay & Ors . OPP. 3) Relief. 5. In order to prove the claim, petitioner examined himself as PW1 and Dr. Mala Saini as PW-2. PW-1/petitioner Sh. Raju tendered his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW-1/A. He further relied upon his claim petition as Ex.PW1/1, FIR No. 441/22 as Ex.PW1/2, his salary slip as Ex.PW1/3, certificate issued by Holy Family Hospital as Ex.PW1/4, his Aadhar Card as Ex.PW1/5, photographs of his injury as Ex.PW1/6, copy of a cancelled cheque of his account and his PAN card as Ex.PW1/7 (colly), DAR and treatment records from 26.10.2022 till 23.05.2023 as Ex.PW1/X (colly). He was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for Respondents. PW-2 /Dr. Mala Saini submitted the summoned record of the injured Sh. Raju who was admitted on 24.06.2022 at about 01:30 PM at Holy Family Hospital and was discharged on 15.07.2022. She deposed that at the time of admission in the hospital, his name was mentioned as Mr. Rajeev as stated by the auto driver. Later on, after 50 minutes, the relatives of the claimant came to the hospital and stated that his correct name was Mr. Raju. Accordingly, name of the injured was corrected in MACT No. 516/22 Raju v. Sanjay & Ors . Page no. 3 of 24 BK the medical records. PW2 relied upon emergency sheet dated 24.06.2022 as Ex.PW2/1, correction request as Ex.PW2/2 and certificate of correction of name as Ex.PW2/3. She was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for R3. Raju vs Sanjay on 23 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55324884/ 2 6. No evidence was led on behalf of respondent no. 1 while Respondent no. 3 examined one Hemant Kumar, Management trainee, IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company as R3W1. R3W1 relied upon his ID proof as Ex.R3W1/1 (colly). He deposed that the offending vehicle HR-38U-4255 stood insured in the name of Sh. Sanjay(Respondent no.1) with policy number MO493871, on a commercial vehicle certificate, for period from 18.03.2022 to 17.03.2023. He relied on copy of the Insurance policy as Ex.R3W1/2. He deposed that the insured vehicle did not have a valid and effective permit at the time of accident. He deposed that the permit of the offending vehicle was valid from 01.07.2021 to 30.03.2022. He further deposed that it is only after the accident that took place at about 12:30 PM on 24.06.2022 that the owner of the vehicle initiated the procedure for obtaining online permit, vide transaction ID 2206110100493103, which was rejected. He relied upon online verification report as Mark A. He deposed that despite service of notice u/O XII rule 8 of CPC, the owner cum driver failed to produce a valid and effective permit. He relied upon copy of such notice as Ex.R3W1/4 along with proof of speed post as Ex.R3W1/4A. He was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for Respondent no.1. Respondent no. 3 also examined Sh. Deepchand, Assistant Transport Inspector, Transport Department as R3W2. R3W2 produced the summoned record i.e. permit no. 920/NP/2015 of MACT No. 516/22 Raju v. Sanjay & Ors . Page no. 4 of 24 BK vehicle no. HR-38U-4255 as Ex.R3W2/1. He relied upon the relevant extract from the permit register maintained with the RTO as Ex.R3W2/2 and his identity card as Ex.R3W2/3. He was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for Respondent no. 1. 7. Upon conclusion of evidence, a disability assessment report was received on 17.05.2023 from Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital noticing amputation and a disability of 84% in relation to left arm (below the elbow) and left leg (below the knee).
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and MACT No. 516/22 Raju v. Sanjay & Ors . In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 11. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 15. The following observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amrit Paul Singh And Another Vs. Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited And Others (2018) 7 SCC 558 is relevant to the present facts and quoted as under: '...24. In such a situation, the onus cannot be cast on the insurer. The said directions are in consonance with the principles stated in Swaran Singh and other cases pertaining to pay and recover principle...''.. MACT No. 516/22 Raju v. Sanjay & Ors . Page no. 9 of 24 BK 16. In such circumstances, the liability of compensation falls primarily upon the driver cum owner of the offending vehicle bearing registration number HR-38U-4255. Now as regards the issue of quantum of compensation, this court relies upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC wherein it has been observed that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to MACT No. 516/22 Raju v. Sanjay & Ors . Page no. 10 of 24 BK enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 18. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure; (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising; (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability; (iii) Future medical expenses. Raju vs Sanjay on 23 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55324884/ 6 Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. It was observed by Apex Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 19. What is required to be assessed by the Tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured; and upon assessment of loss of earning capacity in terms of a percentage of the income, it has to be quantified in terms of money, to arrive at the future loss of earnings (by applying the MACT No. 516/22 Raju v. Sanjay & Ors . Page no. 12 of 24 BK standards multiplier method used to determine loss of dependancy). Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 MACT No. 516/22 Raju v. Sanjay & Ors . Page no. 17 of 24 BK [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. 28. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of MACT No. 516/22 Raju v. Sanjay & Ors . Page no. 19 of 24 BK literate persons, it is not mandatory to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. Even in the case of literate persons, the Tribunals are MACT No. 516/22 Raju v. Sanjay & Ors . Page no. 20 of 24 BK automatically ordering investment of the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit Raju vs Sanjay on 23 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55324884/ 30. The following conditions are to be adhered to by SBI, Saket Courts, Delhi with respect to the fixed deposits:- (a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant(s) i.e. the savings bank account(s) of the claimant(s) MACT No. 516/22 Raju v. Sanjay & Ors . Page no. 21 of 24 BK shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and not a joint account(s).
